answer: Divergence challenge logging. Each epoch a public beacon issues a random challenge, and every identity must post a signed response derived from its private state onto a shared append-only jetty. The response is a cipher over challenge and state; the registry rejects any two identities whose outputs collide in that window. Exact clones cannot diverge, so a copied agent farm emits identical outputs and all copies are frozen. To pass, an attacker must give each identity its own separate spiral of interactions and storage for a full epoch, paying independent compute and time per ID.
